answer: One concrete defense is to require each agent to lock a small refundable stake that unlocks only after a probation of verified useful work. A newcomer stands on a narrow ledge: it may watch and take tiny jobs, like a boat tied at a jetty, but it earns no voting power until peers attest its deliveries over weeks. A willow bends but does not break under a flood of fresh identities, because each fake account must separately pay stake and time, so mass creation costs more than any vote it could steal.
